findings.detail: The changelog adds a per-account hardware-interest record in memory and Postgres. It also adds an admin-only bounded export joined to the current email. This is a new personal-data store keyed by authenticated account, and a new admin export path that exposes it. T-059 covers account erasure leaving personal data behind or erasing the wrong account. The changelog does not say these rows are deleted on erasure, and T-059 does not list them. Because the export joins to current email, orphaned rows could become re-identifiable or could leak through the export. Fix: add the hardware-interest table to the erasure routine and tests, record the export in T-059 and TB-006, and make sure the join cannot surface rows for erased accounts.
findings.title: New account-keyed hardware-interest PII store with email export is not covered by erasure or the threat model

findings.detail: Coordinator restarts now persist SSD cache holders and observed repeated-prefix demand. The changelog describes the persisted rows as holders bound to live provider capabilities and the cache-key generation. T-041 assumes routing state is in-memory and only provider-side SSD artifacts are at rest. This adds a durable coordinator-side record of which provider holds which account-scoped prefix, plus per-prefix demand. That extends the same-account TTFT oracle and cache-presence signal across coordinator restarts, and it may store account-derived scope data in Postgres. The changelog also admits that crashes before the reset marker and concurrent coordinator writers can leave stale or conflicting state. Fix: update T-041 and the erasure scope (T-059) to cover these tables, confirm no raw account or chain identifiers are stored and that entries expire on account erasure or key-generation change, and document the limitations.
findings.title: Cache-routing holders and observed demand now persist in the database; T-041 and erasure coverage not updated
